quiz.q: What does “triple-ζ” (TZ) mean for a basis set?
options: Each valence atomic orbital is described by three basis functions
Each atom carries three polarization functions
The basis set was optimized for third-row atoms
Three Gaussians are contracted into every basis function
quiz.explain: ζ counts how many independent functions describe each valence orbital. Going DZ → TZ → QZ gives the orbitals more flexibility, and usually adds higher angular-momentum polarization functions too.

quiz.q: The basis set incompleteness error (BSIE) comes from…
options: Expanding the orbitals in a finite (truncated) set of functions
Rounding errors in the SCF procedure
Using experimental instead of computed geometries
quiz.explain: A complete basis would need infinitely many functions. Any real basis is a truncation, and the difference from the complete-basis-set (CBS) limit is the BSIE.

quiz.q: In the dimer (HCl)₂, each HCl can “borrow” basis functions centred on its partner. With a small basis, what does this do to the computed binding?
options: Nothing: basis functions on one molecule cannot affect the other
It makes the dimer artificially too stable (overbinding)
It makes the dimer artificially too unstable (underbinding)
It only changes the geometry, not the energy
quiz.explain: This is the basis set superposition error (BSSE). The dimer gets a better description than the isolated monomers, so binding is overestimated. BSSE shrinks as the basis grows, which is one reason the error changes with ζ.
